data_description.output_path: Where the generated YAML is written. What matters is that AppDaemon can read exactly this file – via /share for an add-on, or via a shared mount for separate containers.
data_description.reload_mode: AppDaemon does not notice a changed !include file by itself. "none" = reload manually · "restart_addon" = restart the AppDaemon add-on through the Supervisor (Home Assistant OS/Supervised) · "touch_module" = update the mtime of a file AppDaemon watches (fine-grained, needs file access) · "restart_container" = restart the Docker container through the Docker API. Only the paths that can actually work on the detected installation type are offered.
data_description.reload_addon: Shown in the URL of the add-on page (…/hassio/addon/SLUG/info). For the community "AppDaemon" add-on it is a0d7b954_appdaemon.
data_description.reload_touch_path: AppDaemon's apps.yaml. It has to be that file: touching the app module (apps/nspanel.py) restarts the app but does NOT re-read the configuration pulled in via !include, so the change would stay invisible. Home Assistant must be able to see it. It also requires AppDaemon NOT to run in production mode: with production_mode: true in appdaemon.yaml it stops checking files for changes, so touching has no effect at all – and reports no error. Use restart_container or restart_addon in that case.
data_description.reload_container: Requires /var/run/docker.sock to be mounted into the Home Assistant container.
data_description.backup_count: Before every overwrite the previous state is copied into a "backups" subdirectory next to the output file; older ones are pruned to this count. 0 disables backups – a mistake in the editor is then irreversible.

abort.already_configured: NSPanel UI Config is already set up.
